thread:
incident-bot: [PAGE] SEV2 - 502s observed on /v1/completions from dedicated-gpu-pool (1785001234). Trigger: 502 rate > 5% for 5m. Please ack

alex (eng-sre): Acked. seeing concurrent OOMs on nodes in dedicated-gpu-pool. paging to runtime and infra.

rachel (eng-runtime): Jumping in. Logs show model-worker processes being killed by OOM killer around the same time as autoscaler downsized nodes. Suspect autoscaler scale-in thresholds too aggressive.

devin (eng-platform): Autoscaler events: scale-in at 1785000800 -> removed 2 nodes. Those nodes had long-lived model KV caches. Autoscaler used default utilization metric, not memory-based.

priya (support): Monitoring customer impact now. Early look: a handful of customers saw elevated 502s, retrying; one customer reported a user-facing degradation. Collecting request IDs.

alex (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation: paused autoscaler scale-ins, cordoned questionable node types, and triggered rolling restart of model-workers on remaining nodes to clear broken state. Also temporarily bumped replicas for the deployment.

infra-bot: Autoscaler scaled back to paused mode by devin at 1785002100.

rachel (eng-runtime): After restarts + replica bump we see 502 rate drop to baseline by 1785005400. Heap dumps attached to internal incident doc. Initial hypothesis: scale-in evicted nodes while KV cache still required by active sessions -> memory churn -> OOM -> process restarts -> 502s cascaded.

alex (eng-sre): Can we capture timeline + assign postmortem owners? I'll write the postmortem. Need owners for monitoring, deploy pipeline, autoscaler config, customer outreach, and brown-bag.

devin (eng-platform): I'll own autoscaler config change and add memory-based metric gating (owner: devin, due: 1785080000). Will open PR to adjust scale-in policy and add annotation to prevent removal of nodes with active KV cache.

rachel (eng-runtime): I'll own runtime mitigations: make model-worker more resilient to sudden memory pressure, add defensive guards to prevent OOM loops (owner: rachel, due: 1785065000). Also will add an emergency flag that skips aggressive cache reloads during node churn.

priya (support): I'll draft customer outreach for affected orgs (owner: priya, due: 1785020000). We'll prioritize the one reporting user-facing issues.

alex (eng-sre): Proposed action items:
- A1: Autoscaler scale-in gating on memory + active-kvcache annotation (devin)
- A2: Runtime OOM loop protection + emergency cache-backoff (rachel)
- A3: Canary that simulates node loss under warm cache load (eng-platform)
- A4: Customer outreach + incident timeline (priya)
- A5: Postmortem doc + exec summary (alex)
- A6: Brown-bag session on scale/eviction patterns and prevention (eng-education)

rachel (eng-runtime): Quick config snippet I'll propose for testing in staging:
```
# avoid OOM during scale-in
autoscaler:
  scaleIn:
    enabled: true
    minNodes: 3
    memoryThresholdPercent: 65
    excludeIfAnnotation: "kvcache.active"
```

devin (eng-platform): I'll create a staging test that simulates sudden node removal while synthetic kvcache traffic runs. PR: https://git.redwood/s/repo/pulls/560 (WIP).

alex (eng-sre): Timeline notes (rough):
- 1785000600 first small spike in 502s
- 1785000800 autoscaler scaled in by 2 nodes
- 1785001000 OOMs begin, processes restarted
- 1785001600 on-call paged and mitigation started
- 1785002100 autoscaler paused, replicas bumped
- 1785005400 502 rate normalized

priya (support): Customer impact: 9 orgs saw transient 502s, 2 orgs reported degraded UX with >10s latency spikes. No data exfiltration suspected. Will include request IDs and sample logs in the outreach.

eng-education: We can host the brown-bag. Suggested slot: 1785091200 (Thursday next week 12:00 PT). Format: 20m root cause + 20m demos + 10m Q&A. Recording and slides. Who will present?

tom (product): I'll help co-author the customer-facing summary. Also propose adding this scenario to SLO runbook: explicit guidance for scale-in vs. increasing replicas in face of cache-dependent workloads.

rachel (eng-runtime): For the postmortem bullets from runtime: 1) autoscaler uses CPU util only -> doesn't protect memory-heavy cached workloads; 2) model-worker cache lifecycle isn't tied to node lifecycle; 3) mitigation pattern: prevent scale-in while active caches exist and add cache-backoff on restart.

devin (eng-platform): For platform bullets: 1) Add memory as a first-class metric in autoscaler decisions; 2) annotate pods with kvcache activity so scale-in can respect that; 3) add deployment pre-stop hook that drains or checkpoints cache where possible.

alex (eng-sre): Postmortem plan: I'll draft in /docs/incidents/1785001234-postmortem.md. Deadline for first draft: 1785030000. Please add 2-3 bullets into the doc for your assigned items by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize owners.

priya (support): Draft outreach will be in #support-drafts and I'll ping tom for approvals.

infra-bot: Reminder: create a follow-up ticket in infra board and link to postmortem template: /runbooks/postmortem-template.md

alex (eng-sre): Brown-bag: rachel + devin volunteered to demo. eng-education will schedule and record. Please add slides to the postmortem doc link when ready.

rachel (eng-runtime): One more note: we had a rollback candidate but rollback left KV cache mismatch across nodes; not a safe rollback. Documenting that as a mitigation lesson.

tom (product): Request: include a short customer-facing FAQ entry: "Why did this happen and what are you changing?" I'll draft and add to doc.

alex (eng-sre): Final ask: any additional follow-ups? If not, I'll close the incident channel once the postmortem is filed and owners confirmed.

sre-lead: Thanks for quick mitigation. Please highlight owner SLAs for postmortem and ensure exec summary is ready for the cadence call.

-- end of thread --
